facts.detail: Ofcom published the Connected Nations Spring 2026 update on 13 May 2026.
The publication reports fixed broadband availability and mobile coverage using a January 2026 snapshot.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises, equal to 82% of 30.5 million homes.
Gigabit-capable broadband was available to 27.1 million homes, equal to 89%.
Ofcom reported 39,000 premises unable to access decent broadband from fixed-line or fixed wireless access networks.

facts.detail: The January 2026 collection included submissions from 52 fixed-network and 18 fixed-wireless-access providers.
Ofcom used Ordnance Survey AddressBase Premium and Islands products, Epoch 123, as the premise base.
Ofcom states that the data is supplied on an open basis under the Open Government Licence, subject to its conditions.
The files are supplied as comma-separated values with double-quote text delimiters where applicable.
The official data note identifies a v2 correction dated 7 July 2026.

facts.detail: The postcode field is documented without spaces, for example SE19HA.
The postcode_space field is documented with a single space, for example SE1 9HA.
Postcode files include a postcode-area field, for example SE.
For postcode and output-area levels, Ofcom reports gigabit-capable coverage but not full-fibre coverage because of commercial confidentiality.
Coverage figures refer to fixed-line broadband unless a field description explicitly includes fixed wireless access.

facts.detail: SFBB availability is defined as coverage at 30 Mbit/s or greater.
UFBB 100 Mbit/s availability is defined as coverage at 100 Mbit/s or greater.
UFBB availability is also documented at the 300 Mbit/s-or-greater threshold.
Gigabit availability is the percentage of premises covered by a gigabit-capable service.
Unable-to-receive metrics are documented for 2, 5, 10 and 30 Mbit/s thresholds on matched premises.

facts.detail: Decent broadband is defined using at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
The fixed-or-FWA unable-to-receive field includes fixed broadband, WISP and Mobile FWA availability.
The decent-broadband unable-to-receive measure includes non-matched records and zero predicted speeds.
The FWA decent-broadband field reports premises able to receive at least 10 Mbit/s down and 1 Mbit/s up from a WISP.
The combined schema includes a percentage-of-premises-with-NGA field.

facts.detail: Ofcom's Spring 2026 page exposes the fixed broadband coverage and full-fibre take-up download as a 32.2 MB ZIP.
The official data note covers UK and nations, local authorities, parliamentary and devolved constituencies, output areas and postcodes.
At each detailed geography, Ofcom provides all-premises and residential-premises coverage files.
Ofcom states that the Spring 2026 data was used to update its broadband and mobile coverage checkers.
Ofcom published an interactive report and summary tables alongside the downloadable data.
